metadata.note: The Bessemer and Lake Erie and its predecessors (Shenango and Allegheny; Pittsburgh, Shenango and Lake Erie; and the Pennsylvania Company's 1881 operation of the Meadville Railway), drawn on 2026-10-21 from the research report research/branches/bessemer_and_lake_erie_railroad.txt in the companion site repo. Only the report's drawable spans are drawn; the predecessor eras survive mostly as one-year anchors. Rule 4 splits share geometry: the PS&LE 1891 anchor sits on the B&LE Erie line, the S&A 1873-1880 span on part of the southern main, and the PRR 1881 anchor on the Linesville - Meadville branch. The 1897 PB&LE reorganisation and the 1901 B&LE lease are changes of operating company; the PB&LE era (1897-1901) has no dated passenger source and is not drawn. The B&LE's last passenger train ran 5 March 1955.
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 edition (schedules of 30 Sept 1951), B&LE page - https://archive.org/details/the-official-guide-of-the-railways-images
metadata.geometry_method: Traced with opstrace.py: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (mail.ru mirror, cached degree tiles) plus OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=B&LE (rail-trails included) and OpenHistoricalMap for the lifted Meadville, Hilliards and Mercer stretches. Ways tagged old_railway_operator=B&LE, operator=Canadian National Railway or name=Bessemer Subdivision costed 1x, untagged rail 1.25x, other named operators 12x. Waypoints geocoded with Nominatim (each geocode's type checked; county, township and wrong-place answers hand-pinned) and snapped by a dynamic program; Douglas-Peucker 8 m, then trim_reversals.
not_yet_sourced: OPEN ends: ble-mercer-loop (1940 is the last confirmed year; probably to 17 May 1954) and sa-shenango-harrisville (1880 is the last confirmed year; the S&A ran until January 1888).
ANCHORS: ble-hilliards-branch 1926, psle-erie-greenville 1891, prr-linesville-meadville 1881 - each a single confirmed year.

Not drawn for want of a dated passenger source: the PB&LE era 1897-1901 (whole system); PS&LE 1888-1897 on Shenango - Butler; the PS&LE Erie line 1892-1900; the Conneaut, Meadville and Linesville branches before 1901; Meadville & Linesville 1884-1891; the 1883-1900 Branchton - Butler extension (operator unknown); S&A Harrisville - Hilliards and Greenville - Shenango.
North Bessemer - East Pittsburgh: drawn on Union Railroad track; whether that is the track B&LE trains used, and whether 1951-54 trains still ran beyond North Bessemer, are unresolved.
Greenville - Osgood opening: ICC 1884 vs west2k 17 Dec 1888 - not reconciled. Butler - North Bessemer completion: railfan.com 1897 vs ICC 1901.
Meadville branch end: 17 Jan 1935 (Depot Museum) vs 29 Sept 1935 (west2k) - same year. Park spur 1934 rests on two secondary sources.
Conneaut branch: whether passengers ran to Conneaut Harbor or only to Conneaut town.
Headways other than the 1940 main-line counts and the 1914-16 Meadville count are estimates.
metadata.freight_only_excluded: Not drawn, freight only or no passenger evidence: the K-O cutoff (Osgood - Kremis, 1901-02); the Western Allegheny / Kaylor branch (Queen Junction - Bradys Bend); Hilliards sub-spurs to Goff/Erico and Argentine; Conneaut Harbor ore-dock trackage; all post-passenger freight years (Hilliards after its unknown pre-1940 end, Meadville branch 1935-1977, Linesville leg 1932-1953, Conneaut branch 1932-, whole system 1955-); North Bessemer - Bessemer / Union RR freight connections.

properties.geometry_quality: 61.3 mi drawn Erie (B&LE 12th Street yard) - Greenville against 62.9 mi documented (Fowler mileposts; Feb 1940 Official Guide). Three traced pieces: Erie - Cascade 0.9 mi on ex-B&LE (Erie Terminal) track; Cascade - Wallace Junction 11.9 mi ON THE NICKEL PLATE ALIGNMENT (today Norfolk Southern's Lake Erie District, OSM old_railway_operator=NKP), which the B&LE used by trackage rights / joint operation from 1891 and never owned - drawn on the NKP's own line deliberately, not on the parallel ex-NYC (CSX) main; Wallace Junction - Greenville 48.0 mi entirely on ways OSM tags old_railway_operator=B&LE (CN Bessemer Subdivision / Erie Subdivision / Greenville Line). The pieces meet with connectors of 0.3 km and 0.4 km. No straight-line legs. Every station waypoint (Girard, Albion, Springboro, Conneautville, Shermansville, Hartstown, Adamsville, Osgood) lies within 0.4 km of the line. Drawn via Greenville station, NOT over the 1901-02 K-O freight cutoff at Osgood. The exact B&LE passenger terminal at Erie is placed at the ex-B&LE yard south of 12th Street; the station building's exact site is not sourced.

segments.note: The Bessemer and Lake Erie's northern main line, Greenville - Osgood - Albion - Girard - Wallace Junction - (Nickel Plate trackage rights) - Cascade - Erie. Drawn from 1901, when the B&LE took over operation under its 999-year lease of the Pittsburg, Bessemer and Lake Erie (effective 1 April 1901, ICC valuation); the line carried PS&LE/PB&LE passengers from 1891 (see psle-erie-greenville; 1892-1900 undrawn for want of a dated source). Fowler lists the stations under both his 1901 company timetable and 1926 Official Guide letters. Feb 1940 Official Guide: Nos. 12/13, one round trip daily except Sunday, Erie 3:20 PM -> Greenville 5:25 PM, Greenville 7:20 AM -> Erie 9:25 AM. Sept 1951 Guide: times survive for No. 12 at Osgood - Dicksonburg. Early in the century there were four trains a day North Bessemer - Erie (Akron RR Club, undated). Last train: No. 12 left Greenville 7:30 a.m. Saturday 5 March 1955 for Erie with 200+ riders (Greenville Record-Argus via Akron RR Club; year corroborated by american-rails.com and west2k). Freight continued and continues (CN). Headway is the 1940 count (one train each way a day); earlier service was more frequent but is not dated. avg_speed_kmh is computed from the 1940 schedule (62.9 mi in 2 h 05 min).
sources: Segment-level: Fowler 1901/1926 station letters; Feb 1940 Official Guide Nos. 12/13 with times; Feb 1952 Official Guide (Sept 1951) times on No. 12; last run 5 Mar 1955 per Greenville Record-Argus via Akron RR Club; lease date 1 Apr 1901 per ICC valuation.
Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 edition (schedules of 30 Sept 1951), B&LE page - https://archive.org/details/the-official-guide-of-the-railways-images

properties.geometry_quality: 96.8 mi drawn Greenville - East Pittsburgh against 97.7 mi documented (Feb 1940 Official Guide mileposts 62.9 -> 160.6). Greenville - North Bessemer 88.4 mi entirely on ways OSM tags old_railway_operator=B&LE (today CN's Bessemer Subdivision), via Shenango, Fredonia, Grove City, Branchton, Queen Junction and Butler; no straight-line legs. North Bessemer - East Pittsburgh 8.4 mi: about 1.6 mi of B&LE North Bessemer yard track and then about 6.8 mi on track OSM tags operator=Union Railroad - i.e. THIS FEATURE DRAWS UNION RAILROAD TRACK south of North Bessemer. Whether the B&LE's passenger trains used Union Railroad track here (the ICC records ~8 mi of PB&LE subleased to the Union RR from 2 Apr 1906) or a B&LE alignment now gone is NOT established (report UNRESOLVED 5). MERCER: the main line is drawn on the present direct line between Mercer Junction and Houston Junction (today's CN); the trains themselves called at Mercer by running over the older line through the town (separate feature ble-mercer-loop). When the direct line was built is not sourced, so for early years this may be a LATER alignment than the trains used. Butler: the line is drawn through Butler on the B&LE alignment; the 1914 move of the passenger stop to the B&O Chantler Avenue depot is not modelled. Not drawn: the K-O cutoff (Osgood - Kremis, freight only).

segments.note: The southern main line, Greenville - Shenango - Fredonia - Mercer - Grove City - Branchton - Butler - North Bessemer - East Pittsburgh, where passengers connected with the PRR; B&LE trains never reached downtown Pittsburgh as far as found. Drawn from 1901, when the B&LE began operating under its lease (1 April 1901, ICC). Feb 1940 Official Guide: Nos. 1/2, one round trip daily except Sunday, Greenville 7:00 AM -> Mercer 7:33 -> Butler 8:59 -> North Bessemer 9:59 -> East Pittsburgh 10:25 AM, return 3:45 PM -> Greenville 7:18 PM. Sept 1951 Guide: 'lve. Greenville ... 7:10 PM' survives on the southern section heading. Service between Greenville and North Bessemer ended 17 May 1954 (Greenville Record-Argus via Akron RR Club). Whether the 1951-54 trains still ran beyond North Bessemer to East Pittsburgh is NOT established - the closing notice names only Greenville and North Bessemer - so the North Bessemer - East Pittsburgh stretch's later years rest on this feature's whole-line span, not on a dated source for that stretch. Butler passenger stop moved from the B&LE Center Avenue station to the B&O Chantler Avenue depot in 1914 (west2k). Trains ran via Greenville and Shenango, not over the 1901-02 K-O freight cutoff. Butler - North Bessemer opening date conflicts (railfan.com 1897; ICC 1901) - not material to a 1901 start. Headway is the 1940 count; earlier frequency not dated. avg_speed_kmh is computed from the 1940 schedule (97.7 mi in 3 h 25 min).
sources: Segment-level: Fowler 1901/1926 station letters; Feb 1940 Official Guide Nos. 1/2 with times; Feb 1952 Official Guide (Sept 1951) 7:10 PM time; end 17 May 1954 per Greenville Record-Argus via Akron RR Club; 1914 Butler station change per west2k.
Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 edition (schedules of 30 Sept 1951), B&LE page - https://archive.org/details/the-official-guide-of-the-railways-images

properties.geometry_quality: 4.9 mi drawn Mercer Junction - Mercer - Houston Junction against about 3.5 mi in Fowler's mileposts (Mercer Jct 80.2, Mercer 81.0, Houston Jct 83.7). Traced on the abandoned grade OSM tags railway=abandoned, old_railway_operator=B&LE (the older line through Mercer), no straight-line legs. The drawn length runs about 1.4 mi long because the hand-pinned Mercer Junction point sits north of the true junction, where the old and new lines run side by side; the junction's exact site is not sourced. Fowler marks Mercer '(reverse)' - trains backed in or out; the reversing move is not modelled.

segments.note: The Mercer line: main-line trains left the main at Mercer Junction, called at Mercer (Fowler: 'Mercer (reverse)') and regained the main at Houston Junction. Mercer Jct - Mercer was built by the PS&LE in 1889 (ICC). Drawn from 1901 (B&LE lease; Fowler lists Mercer under 1901 and 1926). Feb 1940: Nos. 1/2 called at Mercer 7:33 AM / 6:43 PM. Around WWI the B&LE moved to the shared PRR station in Mercer and closed its Mercer Jct and Houston Jct stations (west2k). OPEN END: 1940 is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end. The Sept 1951 Guide lists Mercer as a coupon station but no time survives, so 1951 service is neither confirmed nor denied; service probably lasted to 17 May 1954 with the rest of the southern main, but no source says so. Do not extend without evidence. Headway is the 1940 count.
sources: Segment-level: Fowler route 306 ('Mercer (reverse)', 1901/1926); Feb 1940 Official Guide times at Mercer; ICC 1889 build. End year 1940 is last confirmed, not an ending.

properties.geometry_quality: 16.0 mi drawn Meadville Junction - Lynces Junction - Conneaut Lake - Meadville against 15.6 mi documented (Fowler mileposts 5.0 -> 20.6; american-rails.com). The branch was lifted in 1977. Traced on ways OSM tags railway=abandoned, old_railway_operator=B&LE (Meadville Jct - Conneaut Lake - Custards), then the Ernst Trail rail-trail on the B&LE grade into Meadville, then surviving ex-B&LE track (now Western New York and Pennsylvania) to Mead Avenue. APPROXIMATED: about 0.8 mi straight line north of the Ernst Trail covered bridge, where the trail leaves the grade and the grade itself is not mapped, and a 0.5 km connector west of Conneaut Lake where two OSM grade fragments do not join. The Meadville station point (Mead Avenue) is hand-placed; its exact site is not sourced.

segments.note: Meadville Junction - Lynces Junction - Conneaut Lake - West Vernon - Mercer Pike - Meadville (Mead Avenue), the Meadville, Conneaut Lake and Linesville, leased to the PS&LE from 1 July 1891 and operated by the B&LE from 1 April 1901 (MCL&L stayed owner until the 1949 merger - an ownership change, not an operator change). Drawn from 1901; 1891-1900 PS&LE/PB&LE service is undated and undrawn. 1914-16: four trains each way, with a McKeen gasoline motor car tried briefly (Meadville Railroad Depot Museum). 'Passenger service from Meadville to Meadville Junction was abandoned on January 17, 1935' (Depot Museum); west2k has Meadville Junction station closed to passengers 29 September 1935 - same year, recorded as a conflict of dates. Feb 1940 Guide prints the branch as a station list with no trains, Meadville and Mercer Pike freight-only. Freight to 13 May 1977. Headway is the 1914-16 count (four each way, about every 6 hours over a day) and is not dated for other years.
sources: Segment-level: Fowler route 308 (1901/1926); 1914-16 schedule and 17 Jan 1935 end per Meadville Railroad Depot Museum (FCVRRHS) timeline; 29 Sept 1935 Meadville Jct closure per west2k Crawford Co. - local-history sources, not primary.

Do not widen this anchor without a dated source. Probably a mixed train - not established. Headway is an ESTIMATE and is NOT sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: 30.0 mi drawn Shenango - Harrisville. Traced entirely on ways OSM tags old_railway_operator=B&LE: the present CN line Shenango - Mercer Junction, the abandoned older line through Mercer to Houston Junction, then CN through Pardoe and Grove City to the line's nearest point to Harrisville. LATER ALIGNMENT RISK: this is the B&LE-era alignment. Whether the 1869-76 Shenango and Allegheny ran on exactly this line (including the Mercer route) is not sourced, and any later realignments around Grove City and Branchton are not identified. No straight-line legs. The S&A's own Shenango - Greenville line (1882) and its pre-1882 use of Atlantic & Great Western track into Greenville are not drawn (no confirmed passenger years).

segments.note: The Bessemer and Lake Erie's earliest predecessor: Shenango - Fredonia - Mercer - Pardoe - Pine Grove (Grove City) - Harrisville. Opened Shenango - Pardoe October 1869, Harrisville July 1872, Hilliards January 1876 (american-rails.com; Wikipedia). Drawn 1873-1880, the span between the first and last dated touch-downs: in 1873 'around 18 S&A trains per day' left the Atlantic & Great Western depot at Greenville (west2k Mercer) - possibly including coal trains, a medium-low-confidence figure; Harrisville had a station 'as early as 1874'; the S&A's 1880 timetable shows Pine Grove (west2k). OPEN END: 1880 is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end - the S&A ran (under receivers from 15 March 1884) until reorganised as the PS&LE on 12 January 1888, but no later year is dated. Do not extend without evidence. Not drawn: 1869-72 (no dated passenger source), Harrisville - Hilliards (no touch-down of its own), and Greenville - Shenango, which the S&A ran over A&GW track until opening its own line on 11 March 1882. Headway derives from the 1873 '18 trains' figure and is an ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: west2k Mercer Co. station histories (1873 trains, 1874 Harrisville station, 1880 timetable); american-rails.com opening dates; PRR chronology 1882. End year 1880 is last confirmed, not an ending.

Waypoints geocoded with Nominatim (each geocode's type checked; county, township and wrong-place answers hand-pinned) and snapped by a dynamic program; Douglas-Peucker 8 m, then trim_reversals.
properties.geometry_quality: 20.4 mi drawn Linesville - Meadville against 20.6 mi documented (Fowler). Geometry is the concatenation of ble-linesville-meadville-junction and ble-meadville-branch (see their geometry_quality, including the ~0.8 mi straight line north of the Ernst Trail covered bridge). LATER ALIGNMENT RISK: Meadville Junction did not exist in 1881 (the Erie line came in 1891); the 1881 Meadville Railway is assumed to have run on the same grade, which is not sourced.

segments.note: The Meadville Railway, Linesville - Shermansville - Conneaut Lake (Evansburg) - Mercer Pike - Meadville, operated at first by the PRR-controlled Erie & Pittsburgh / Pennsylvania Company (PRR Lines West), coloured as the PRR under Rule 4. 'Oct. 3, 1881: The Erie & Pittsburgh ran its first train from Linesville to Meadville'; the station opened and full operations began 20 Oct 1881 (Meadville Railroad Depot Museum). ANCHOR: 1881 is the single CONFIRMED passenger year. The Pennsylvania Company's operation lasted until the road was foreclosed and reorganised as the Meadville & Linesville on 3 January 1884; service certainly ran wider, but nothing else in 1881-1900 is dated (Meadville & Linesville 1884-91 and the PS&LE lease from 1 July 1891 are undrawn). Do not widen this anchor without a dated source. Headway is an ESTIMATE and is NOT sourced.
sources: Segment-level: Meadville Railroad Depot Museum (FCVRRHS) timeline - first train 3 Oct 1881. Headway NOT sourced.
